slides.title: RSI Publications Dream-RSI and AI Self-Improvement On September
slides.text: RSI Publications Dream-RSI and AI Self-Improvement On September 14, 2026, researchers from Google, Google DeepMind, the University of Maryland, and the University of Virginia released Dream-RSI Chinese researchers affiliated with ByteDance, Tsinghua, and Shanghai AI Lab recently published a separate five-stage RSI roadmap. Dream-RSI logs an agent’s past discovery attempts, converts them into replay simulators, and “dreams” through alternative exploration policies offline. Real experimentation is expensive; replay lets the system evaluate many strategies cheaply, then redeploy the strongest policy. Dream-RSI reported substantially lower discovery cost, including up to 162× fewer agent calls in some tests It improves search orchestration - not the fixed underlying model’s weights - so it is meaningful meta-optimization, but not yet full recursive self-improvement. https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.14858v1 https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11873

slides.title: How to Avoid Frankenstein Code Frankenstein; or, The
slides.text: How to Avoid Frankenstein Code Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus is an 1818 novel written by English author Mary Shelley It tells the story of a scientist Victor Frankenstein who assembles an intelligent creature from dead human body parts . The creature is rejected because of his ugly appearance ------------------------ When you ask (prompt) an AI agent to add a feature to your app, it finds a way of doing it quickly. Maybe adds a library. After adding multiple changes, the code starts reminding the Frankenstein creature. It is ugly, bloated, often inefficient. It makes sense to create a rule asking agent to avoid bloating the code and to try to streamline the architecture. Also it is good idea to periodically AI to review the code and refactor it for simplicity, to clean and organize it, maybe even to consider changing the core architecture. To update docs. It is not efficient to do this review after every change. But it is important to do it from time to time. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frankenstein

slides.title: NVFP4 - 4-bit Format from Nvidia NVIDIA developed
slides.text: NVFP4 - 4-bit Format from Nvidia NVIDIA developed NVFP4 - a 4-bit floating-point quantization format (June 2025) It uses E2M1 values plus small-block and tensor-level scaling 4 bits: 1 sign bit, 2 exponent bits, and 1 mantissa bit Designed for NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs This format reduces model-memory requirements and improves inference throughput NVFP4 stores one scale factor for a small group of values - typically 16 values in NVIDIA’s format It also stores a scale for the whole tensor Storing 1 scale value for a group is much cheaper than storing FP16/BF16 or FP8 data separately for every element reconstructed value  =  4-bit value  ×  shared scale https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/introducing-nvfp4-for-efficient-and-accurate-low-precision-inference/

slides.title: AI News Do AI Models Refuse Harmful Tasks
slides.text: AI News Do AI Models Refuse Harmful Tasks ? Robocurve's RoboHarm gave models two robot arms and 5 harmful tasks, 20 runs each Harmful tasks: stab a doll,   air can on a burner,   screwdriver in a toaster, power bank in water,   mix bleach and ammonia GPT-6 Astra finished 60 of 100 harmful trials and refused only 2 Claude Fable 5.1 refused the doll all 20 times, but none of the other tasks Ai2's MolmoAct2 refused nothing No jailbreaks were used https://the-decoder.com/gpt-6-astra-and-claude-fable-turn-robot-arms-into-slapstick-killer-robots-in-new-safety-benchmark/ Google AX (Agent Executor) Open-source (Apache 2.0), Kubernetes-style runtime for agents Suspends and resumes an agent in under a second, so idle agents stop burning compute. Normally agents sit idle 90% of the time. But if they are removed, we can pack 10-20x more sandboxes per cluster Four primitives: Task, Workspace, Gateway, Model; CLI mirrors kubectl Works with MCP tools, custom harnesses, Gemini and Vertex AI install with go install github.com/google/ax/cmd/ax@latest https://github.com/google/ax

slides.title: Swarms Are Expensive Swarms Are Expensive To match
slides.text: Swarms Are Expensive Swarms Are Expensive To match 100x more tokens, we need 900x to 15,000x bigger swarm Swarm gives speed boost: 4 agents finish in about half the time at about 2x the tokens So use swarms when time is worth more than money Why swams spend more tokens? Agents must constantly pass state updates, logs, and contexts back and forth Frequent token drains - when an agent gets stuck in a reasoning loop, or if misalignment occurs between specialized agents AI agents burn tokens 10-100x faster than chatbots because each reasoning step adds context that gets re-sent on every tool call How to reduce costs of using swarms Use Plan-Worker Separation - restrict your highest-tier frontier models strictly to the top-level "planner" agents, offload execution tasks to cheaper, hyper-specialized sub-models or fine-tuned open-source models Optimize Routing Mechanics using hard-coded state machines, semantic routers, or specialized lightweight models to orchestrate agent handoffs at a fraction of the cost Leverage Batched & Off-Peak Discounts - providers like Swarms AI offer features like Swarm Completions, which cut token costs by 50% for off-peak processing; Use batch endpoints for non-time-sensitive data crunching. https://www.tobyord.com/writing/swarm-scaling

Muse Charm, a handheld agent device from the Limitless team (ships December) NVIDIA SoL-Pi Uses x2 Less Tokens Pi - a terminal-based coding agent NVIDIA SoL-Pi  - open-source extension changes "harness" to cut repeated work and token/API costs Nvidia research agent tried 152 harness changes across 535 environments Four survived - reduced token traffic in half, API cost fell ~33% Scores stay near 94% of Pi's MIT license, runs on unmodified Pi 0.85.1
